discussion_comments.comment_body:
Not a leak — the storage layer already guarantees a `content_hidden` entry carries no content by the time it reaches the UI.

- `framework/logstore/payload.go:110-145` — `ClearPayload` zeroes every content column, including `raw_request`, `raw_response`, `passthrough_request_body`, `passthrough_response_body`, `params`, `tools`, `tool_calls`, and the OCR/speech/image/video fields.
- `framework/logstore/hybrid.go:236-244` — `prepareDBEntry` calls `ClearPayload` and blanks `content_summary` for hidden entries, with no exclusion-list carve-outs.
- `framework/logstore/hybrid.go:414-416` — reads never rehydrate: `if log == nil || !log.HasObject || log.ContentHidden { return }`.
- `plugins/logging/main.go:1399` — `attachLogRedactionData(ctx, entry, policy.visible())` already withholds reveal mappings.

So there is no API path that returns those payload fields for a hidden entry. In the retain-in-object-storage case content is stripped at write and never hydrated back; in the default disabled case it is never captured at all. The message/OCR/speech/image/video views, Copy request body, Export as JSON, and the Raw JSON tab all operate on the `log` object the UI already holds — an object with no content in it — so gating them on `!log.content_hidden` would add conditionals implying a leak the storage layer prevents. If that guarantee ever regresses, the fix belongs in the Go layer, not in the JSX.

The role filter is hidden only because it has nothing to filter. The banner now uses the same dashed empty-state style as the other tabs.

Resolved on the backend rather than in the UI.

Revoke is destructive cleanup — `RevokeOAuth2Session` only stamps `revoked_at` and never acts under the grant's identity — so we removed the user-mode owner gate from `revokeSession`. Authorization is now by DAC visibility alone (the scoped `GetOAuth2SessionByID` load; `RevokeOAuth2Session` itself is unscoped, so that read is the gate). This matches the existing per-user MCP session revoke, which has never been owner-gated.

So anyone who can see a grant — its owner, a team lead, or an admin — can revoke it across all modes, and the 403 is gone. The Revoke action therefore no longer needs to be hidden or disabled.

Re-authentication stays gated to the bound user, since that path *does* mint credentials under the user's identity; revoke does not. Could you re-check and resolve if this looks right?

The child oauth-discover-callback/layout.tsx repeats the parent's useRbac(UserProvisioning, View) check. While technically redundant given the parent gate, this is a defense-in-depth pattern that's consistent across the SCIM routes, and removing it is a style/judgment call, not a correctness issue.
